observation.visible_scene: A top-down static view of a wooden floor covered with an elaborate arrangement of colorful rectangular domino-like blocks laid out in chains. Several chains rest on small elevated white-and-brown stands (little bridges), while others lie directly on the floor. The chains form a connected network: a long flat zigzag on the far right, a top-left cluster, an upper-left diagonal run, a top-middle run, a right-middle run, a bottom-left run on a stand, a central vertical run, and a lower-right curved loop. The floor planks and lighting are unchanged across all frames, indicating a fixed camera.
visible_changes: Lower-right curved loop (blue/green/yellow/orange/magenta): the magenta and orange upright blocks at its right end topple to lie flat between about t=0.6 and t=0.8.
Top-middle chain: the orange and yellow upright blocks at its right end (next to the brown end-block) fall over between about t=1.0 and t=1.2.
Upper-left diagonal chain (pink/red/orange/yellow): a toppling wave passes through it between about t=1.4 and t=1.7, leaving the run flattened.
Bottom-left elevated stand: the magenta upright block at the right end of the stand's chain falls to lie flat between about t=1.8 and t=2.0.
Top-left cluster: a block near the left end tilts/falls around t=1.6-2.0.
Overall pattern: different chains collapse one after another in sequence, consistent with a propagating domino cascade, rather than all at once.

Persistent/static elements: the far-right long zigzag chain on its white stand, the leftmost floor chain, the central vertical blue chain, and all the white/brown stands themselves remain in place and upright throughout the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The initial disturbance or contact that started any toppling is not shown; the first frame already has some chains standing and the cascade appears underway.
The final resting state of every chain after t=2.67 is not shown; some chains are still upright at the last frame.
uncertain_details: Exact ordering and timing of the smaller topplings (e.g., the top-left cluster vs. the upper-left diagonal) is hard to pin down frame-by-frame.
Some blocks are placed at an angle as part of a curve; distinguishing an angled-but-standing block from one mid-fall is not always clear.
Whether the brown end-blocks on the stands ever move is not clearly supported within this excerpt.
